name: Resident Stamp (Spouse of Anguillian/Belonger)

qualifying_event.description: A person married to an Anguillian citizen or Belonger may apply to the Immigration Department for a Resident Stamp.
qualifying_event.evidence_hint: Marriage certificate, passport, birth certificate, divorce decree (if applicable).

requirements.blocker_text: Requires being married to an Anguillian citizen or Belonger, proven by marriage certificate, passport, and birth certificate (plus divorce decree if applicable).

evidence_required.document: First-time processing fee: EC$200.00; grant of stamp: EC$300.00 (renewal processing: EC$50.00; grant of renewal: EC$200.00)

outcome.duration_length: not specified in the source reviewed (a renewal fee schedule confirms it is time-limited)

sources.title: Government of Anguilla -- Resident Stamps: eligibility (spouse of an Anguillian/Belonger), documents, and fee schedule (as of 1 May 2007)

notes: NEW ROUTE, part of Anguilla's initial build. This is a distinct, lesser interim spousal status from full Belonger Status by marriage (see ai_belonger_status_marriage.json), which instead requires 5 years of marriage and grants a much fuller set of rights -- switchable_to reflects that a Resident Stamp holder can, after accumulating the required years of marriage, separately apply for Belonger Status. The fee figures in the source are explicitly dated 'as of May 1, 2007' -- flagged as likely outdated rather than silently treated as current. work_rights is set to 'none' because the source does not describe the stamp as conferring any work authorisation (a Resident Stamp holder would still need to separately obtain a work permit, per ai_work_permit.json) -- this is inferred from the absence of any statement to the contrary, not an explicit confirmation, and should be treated as an open question. Whether children/other dependants can be included on this status is not addressed in the source.
